title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Appendix C: DNA as Evidence
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Appendix C: Prof. Pacifico A. Agabin on DNA as evidence — its scientific basis and admissibility in Philippine courts
sub_topics: DNA analysis in People v. Vallejo (per curiam death affirmance)
Scientific reliability and admissibility (Daubert v. Merrell Dow)
Chain of custody and probative value of DNA

people: Pacifico A. Agabin (UP College of Law)

stances.claim: DNA evidence, when scientifically reliable and properly handled, is a powerful and admissible tool — as in People v. Vallejo.

notable_anecdotes: Gerrico Vallejo was convicted partly on a DNA match from vaginal swabs (G.R. No. 144656).
one_paragraph_summary: Appendix C reproduces Prof. Pacifico A. Agabin's essay on DNA as evidence. Using People v. Vallejo — where a DNA match helped affirm a death sentence — he discusses the scientific basis, reliability, and admissibility of DNA evidence (invoking Daubert v. Merrell Dow), along with chain-of-custody and constitutional concerns.
